title: Bots get confused more than people
content:
Bots are great until you realize you become a servant to them. I ask for payroll review and I need to login daily because it is not capable of holding credentials. A safety feature that fails the usefulness test.

I’ve been working on a single task for almost 3 hours now. Just asking it to respond to some notes from my accountant and make some QuickBooks updates.

Maybe ungrateful because that’s an amazing thing to begin with. But when there are authentication gates, long delays without asking for help, or not finishing tasks accurately or efficiently the usefulness breaks down.

I downloaded dr eggbot to help. It started out good but now it’s spinning on trying to fix the bots as well.

They aren’t learning. Maybe it’s me but I’m trying and it’s not helping. They are very capable idiots. Training models need significant improvement to really be useful.

I say this as someone who is advocating for this to others. Big fan of SpaceXi.

author: Jonnny B

title: Great but…
content:
Love this AI Agent. Best in the market in terms of ease of use and cross-device compatibility. I’ve tried a bunch of these tools, and Grubbot is probably the closest I’ve found to something I can actually use throughout the day instead of just playing around with.

The biggest pain points are around persistence and intelligence when completing tasks. It still gives up too easily sometimes, gets stuck on things a human would work around, or needs me to jump back in and point it in the right direction. Obviously credit usage is a big limitation as well if you’re trying to use it as more than an occasional tool.

I’m trying to use it almost exclusively now for execution, while pairing it with a larger language model to handle the more complex thinking and heavy lifting. That setup works pretty well. I can use the LLM to think through what needs to happen, then hand the actual task over to Grubbot to go do the work across different apps and devices.

I really hope the developers keep pushing hard on making it smarter, more persistent, and better at figuring things out on its own. That’s the biggest opportunity here. I don’t want an AI that needs to be managed every few steps. I want to give it an outcome and have it keep working until the job is actually done.

Right now it feels more like a high school-level intern than an actual employee.

title: It just works
content:
I’ve been intrigued by agentic AI all year, but found OpenClaw/Hermes style harnesses technically intimidating, and wasn’t confident in my ability to implement them securely. Grok Bot solves that.

Within 10 minutes I’d created my Chief of Staff, and within the first 24 hours my team had accomplished weeks of productive output. I sincerely think it might be the most useful technology I’ve ever used.

Every bot has a sandboxed virtual machine that exists steady-state in the cloud. This lets it do anything you as a human can do on its own web browser and desktop environment — but without the security implications of letting it drive your personal computer.

It’s wild to watch my bots actually clicking around on their own computers screens, or see them collaboratively converse with each other or two solve problems for me. They aren’t quite perfect yet and occasionally still require correction and coaching (you can even share screen recordings to train it to do specific tasks for you). But even fresh bots are impressively competent office workers — moreso than many real humans I’ve hired.

Grok Bot feels like a true iPhone moment for agentic AI. It just works — with zero technical barrier to implementation.

xAI has changed the game, and I expect the other frontier labs to follow with similar products soon.

If you’ve been waiting to get started with AI, now is the time to jump on the train. You will be shocked at how easy this is to use.

The $40 SuperGrok plan is an INSANE value, bundling Grok Bot  with Grok 4.6 + Grok Build, the “expert” version of Grok chat, and ad-free X Premium. If you can’t get this subscription to quickly and easily pay for itself in real-world productivity, then YOU are the problem. For all but the most technical of power users, this is truly the one AI subscription to rule them all.

Welcome to the future.

title: I want to like this.
content:
I paid for and used this and want to like it but can’t. I’m a business owner and would use it as such. There’s a lot of things that need to be fixed before it’s worth the $60 or $200.

1). It’s not even clear what the usage is and how it’s calculated. Your bots doing their job obviously takes up the usage but so does them just talking. When they are in a group take you will have them saying the most useless things which all takes up usage and costs you money. Things like “I have nothing to add” or “I’ll keep quiet” or “the other bot can handle that. It’s not my job”. Like why is any of that needed. It’s almost like X programmed the bots to talk more just to cost the customer more money.

2). There’s no human customer support like at all. It’s impossible to get humans to help you with anything. They have a AI bot customer support that emails you. And no matter what you do the AI bot will not connect you to humans or tell you how to connect to human customer support. If I’m paying $200 I better get some top notch customer support.

3). The bots workflow is so unoptimized and buggy. When you give them a task they will perform it in their “computer” which works but it takes them multiple tries. IE they will send a email either an attachment. Attachment is broken. So they resend it too more times. All while my customer is getting spammed and the bot and costing me more on my usage. The pages on their computer are constantly breaking and timing out. Causing the bot to need to refresh. Again each tome it happens it’s costing you more money literally.

These bots are not good quality and way to unoptimized to be considered anything other then alpha stage. Which wouldn’t be bad if you weren’t being charged an arm and a leg to use them as if they are some top quality AI that has been ironed out.

I want to like this. And I would be lying if I said the bots havnt been useful. But I can’t use an app that costs so much. Only to have the bots waste usage so I have to pay even more to top up and continue their work. They are literally hemorrhaging me money at this point. I paid $60. And burned through that usage in less then 3 hours. Most of it on tasks that had to repeated numerous times just to be completed.

Do better. And until the. Stop charging like your bots are state of the art.

title: Blown away so far!
content:
I did the free trial, which was a little tricky to figure out how to do. On the website if you choose the upgrade to Cursor Ultra option, after clicking on that, even though it said it was $200, it gave me the option for a free trial. The free trial was enough usage to do a decent test with a handful of bots on different tasks.

I ran out of the free usage and based on the results of one bot I had trained on adding product pages to my website, I decided to pay $200 to upgrade to the monthly cursor ultra plan.

So far Grok Bots seem really powerful and capable. I’m really impressed with what it has done so far. Still super early, which means it will only get better. I will have to see how things are running after I have trained all of the bots I’ve created for different tasks, but I feel like this really could be life-changing for me. I have it doing several things that are giving me time back in my day already. And I’m accomplishing more.

Adding product pages to the site has still been on the slow side. About 30 minutes per product page. But I have it telling me how long it is taking it to do each page and it seems to be getting faster. It’s great that I can show it what to do as well. I’m going to show it an optimized workflow for the things. I’m having it do. The initial product adding it did, I didn’t even show out what to do, it just figured everything out. Takes correction really well and now seems to be doing new product pages about as well as I do.

I’ve had my mind blown over and over again using Grok Bot these last couple of days. $200 a month feels expensive, but I think it’s going to enable me to make more money in my small business and recover time. And I’ve had years and years of not having the time I want.

Very well done Grok Bot team!

title: Scott Brady
content:
Don't be fooled by the cute little agents. Grok Bot is for developers.

Until now it was a two-horse race between Claude Code and ChatGPT Codex. Both of those tools create agents that live in a folder (.agents or .claude). You talk to them by opening a session for a given idea or feature. Agents are not sessions.

Grok Bot flips that. Sessions ARE agents. I didn't get it at first. It's a mental shift, and once you make it, everything changes.

I still use the agents I already had in my git repo. Jarvis is still my chief of staff. I pulled him into Grok Bot just by asking. Then I asked him to pull in my other skills, and he did. I asked him to keep them in sync with the git repo, and he says they will. Those skills are my core team.

Now, when I want to explore a new idea and ship it, I hire a new agent in Grok Bot. That specialist has access to my core team. This morning I created one to explore an idea for my software company. It researched the idea and wrote a spec in my labs repository (that's my brain). Then I asked the same agent to start implementing it in another repo where I keep my code. As I iterate, it keeps the spec and the code in sync.

What surprised me: the coding gets kicked off in a Cursor cloud session. I get a link, and I can watch it. The cloud session does the heavy coding. The Grok Bot agent is the orchestrator.

I think this is the moment Grok comes from behind and takes the lead. It has the compute to train smarter models and run agentic workflows faster. Add TerraFab, and eventually the Dyson Swarm. The future is going to be amazing. I've picked my horse.
